items.labelEn: Shortest isolated attosecond light pulse measured (record reported in 2017)
items.labelFr: Plus courte impulsion de lumière attoseconde isolée mesurée (record annoncé en 2017)
items.conditions: Soft-X-ray pulse produced from a two-cycle mid-infrared laser, measured by attosecond streaking (ETH Zurich). Range is the stated ±1 as uncertainty.
items.conditionsFr: Impulsion de rayons X mous produite par un laser infrarouge moyen de deux cycles, mesurée par « streaking » attoseconde (ETH Zurich). La plage correspond à l’incertitude annoncée de ±1 as.
items.quote: We extract an SXR pulse duration of (43±1) as from our streaking measurements, defining a new world record.
items.confidenceNotes: Primary peer-reviewed measurement. 'Record' is as claimed in 2017; I did not verify whether a shorter isolated pulse has been reported since. Value read in the abstract (publisher page blocked by CAPTCHA).

items.labelFr: Première impulsion de lumière attoseconde isolée (2001)
items.conditions: Single extreme-ultraviolet pulse isolated by Ferenc Krausz's group in Vienna in 2001; work recognised by the 2023 Nobel Prize in Physics.
items.conditionsFr: Impulsion unique dans l’ultraviolet extrême isolée par l’équipe de Ferenc Krausz à Vienne en 2001 ; travaux récompensés par le prix Nobel de physique 2023.
items.locator: Press release, paragraph on Agostini and Krausz
items.quote: it possible to isolate a single light pulse that lasted 650 attoseconds.
items.confidenceNotes: Authoritative secondary (Nobel committee) summary of Hentschel et al., Nature 414, 509 (2001); same value in the scientific background (p. 5).

items.labelEn: Atomic unit of time (natural time scale of an electron in an atom)
items.labelFr: Unité atomique de temps (échelle de temps naturelle d’un électron dans un atome)
items.conditions: CODATA 2022 recommended value, 2.418 884 326 5864(26) × 10^-17 s; the intrinsic time scale of electron dynamics in atoms.
items.conditionsFr: Valeur recommandée CODATA 2022, 2,418 884 326 5864(26) × 10^-17 s ; échelle de temps intrinsèque de la dynamique des électrons dans les atomes.
items.locator: CODATA value page 'atomic unit of time', Numerical value
items.confidenceNotes: Physical constant, very high confidence. The gloss 'natural time scale of electrons' follows the Nobel 2023 scientific background ('the intrinsic atomic unit of time, about 24 attoseconds'). The NIST page gives the value only, not this interpretation.

items.labelEn: Delay between two electrons leaving a neon atom (photoelectric effect)
items.labelFr: Décalage entre deux électrons qui quittent un atome de néon (effet photoélectrique)
items.conditions: Neon ionised by 100 eV photons: the 2p electron leaves 21 as later than the 2s electron (Schultze et al., Science 2010), measured with attosecond streaking.
items.conditionsFr: Néon ionisé par des photons de 100 eV : l’électron 2p part 21 as après l’électron 2s (Schultze et al., Science 2010), mesure par « streaking » attoseconde.
items.quote: The 2p electron is slower to leave the neon atom than the 2s electron by 21 as.
items.confidenceNotes: Single landmark experiment; the same source notes theory gave values about a factor of two shorter, so the absolute value was debated. Good as an order of magnitude.

items.labelFr: Une oscillation de la lumière rouge
items.conditions: Red light of wavelength about 700 nm, which oscillates about 430 thousand billion (4.3 × 10^14) times per second; period = 1 / frequency.
items.conditionsFr: Lumière rouge de longueur d’onde d’environ 700 nm, qui oscille environ 430 000 milliards (4,3 × 10^14) de fois par seconde ; période = 1 / fréquence.
items.locator: Heading 'Shorter pulses with the help of high overtones', first paragraph
items.quote: it cycles at about four hundred and thirty thousand billion times per second
items.confidenceNotes: Calculated from an approximate frequency ('about'); 2 significant figures meaningful (≈2.3 fs). The 700 nm wavelength is stated in the same sentence.

items.labelEn: One stretching vibration of the O–H bonds in a water molecule
items.labelFr: Une vibration d’élongation des liaisons O–H d’une molécule d’eau
items.conditions: Isolated water molecule (gas phase). Value: symmetric stretch at 3657 cm^-1; low: antisymmetric stretch at 3756 cm^-1. Period = 1 / (c × wavenumber).
items.conditionsFr: Molécule d’eau isolée (phase gazeuse). Valeur : élongation symétrique à 3657 cm^-1 ; borne basse : élongation antisymétrique à 3756 cm^-1. Période = 1 / (c × nombre d’onde).
items.locator: Table 'Vibrational and/or electronic energy levels', modes 1 (Sym str) and 3 (Anti str)
items.confidenceNotes: Wavenumbers are accurate (0–1 cm^-1); the calculation is exact. In liquid water hydrogen bonding lowers the O–H stretch (broad band), making the period slightly longer; not covered by this source. Consistent with the Nobel 1999 statement that a molecular vibration typically takes 10–100 fs. Quote is the table row for mode 1; mode 3 row reads '3 Anti str 3756 A 3755.79 gas'.

items.labelEn: A broken hydrogen bond in liquid water reforms within
items.labelFr: Une liaison hydrogène rompue dans l’eau liquide se reforme en moins de
items.conditions: Room-temperature liquid water (HOD in D2O for the 2D infrared experiment; molecular-dynamics simulations for the 200 fs figure). Upper bound: virtually all molecules find a new partner within this time.
items.conditionsFr: Eau liquide à température ambiante (HOD dans D2O pour l’expérience infrarouge 2D ; simulations de dynamique moléculaire pour le chiffre de 200 fs). Borne supérieure : presque toutes les molécules retrouvent un partenaire dans ce délai.
items.locator: Abstract; also Results ('Broken hydrogen bonds that persist for 1 ps or longer are extremely rare')
items.quote: virtually all molecules return to a hydrogen-bonding partner within 200 fs.
items.confidenceNotes: Upper bound, not a mean lifetime; the figure comes from simulation, supported qualitatively by 2D-IR experiments. Moderate confidence. | Maintainer curation 2026-11-27: "within 200 fs" is an upper bound: encoded as high.

items.labelEn: Breaking of a chemical bond, watched live (ICN molecule)
items.labelFr: Rupture d’une liaison chimique observée en direct (molécule ICN)
items.conditions: Photodissociation of iodine cyanide, ICN → I + CN, observed by Ahmed Zewail's team with femtosecond laser pulses (Nobel Prize in Chemistry 1999).
items.conditionsFr: Photodissociation du cyanure d’iode, ICN → I + CN, observée par l’équipe d’Ahmed Zewail avec des impulsions laser femtoseconde (prix Nobel de chimie 1999).
items.quote: the I-C bond was about to break: the whole reaction takes place in 200 femtoseconds.
items.confidenceNotes: Authoritative summary of Zewail's first experiments. The press release does not date the ICN experiment itself; era = date of the source (1999). The primary paper should be added if an experiment date is wanted.

items.labelEn: First chemical step of vision (retinal changes shape)
items.labelFr: Première étape chimique de la vision (le rétinal change de forme)
items.conditions: Cis-trans isomerisation of retinal in rhodopsin, the pigment of the rods of the eye, measured by femtosecond spectroscopy.
items.conditionsFr: Isomérisation cis-trans du rétinal dans la rhodopsine, le pigment des bâtonnets de l’œil, mesurée par spectroscopie femtoseconde.
items.quote: With femtosecond spectroscopy other researchers have found that the process takes 200 fs
items.confidenceNotes: Nobel committee summary of other groups' work; primary paper not cited on the page. Era = date of the source. Order of magnitude reliable.

items.labelEn: First charge separation in photosynthesis (photosystem II)
items.labelFr: Première séparation de charges de la photosynthèse (photosystème II)
items.conditions: Isolated photosystem II reaction centre (D1/D2-cyt b559) at ambient temperature, two-dimensional electronic spectroscopy with modelling.
items.conditionsFr: Centre réactionnel isolé du photosystème II (D1/D2-cyt b559) à température ambiante, spectroscopie électronique bidimensionnelle et modélisation.
items.locator: Abstract; Results (Fig. 3a: components 132 fs, 1.5 ps, 13.9 ps)
items.quote: occurs on a time scale of 1.5 ps under ambient conditions.
items.confidenceNotes: Single study; the same paper cites other analyses with components of 400 fs and 1.8 ps, and a faster <200 fs component. Contested assignment; treat as order of magnitude (about 1 ps).

items.labelEn: A water molecule switches hydrogen-bond partner
items.labelFr: Une molécule d’eau change de partenaire de liaison hydrogène
items.conditions: Bulk liquid water at room temperature; time scale of hydrogen-bond exchange, matching the ~2.5 ps reorientation (anisotropy decay) measured by ultrafast infrared spectroscopy.
items.conditionsFr: Eau liquide à température ambiante ; échelle de temps de l’échange de liaisons hydrogène, cohérente avec la réorientation d’environ 2,5 ps mesurée par spectroscopie infrarouge ultrarapide.
items.locator: Section 'Spectral Diffusion and H-Bond Dynamics'; also 'Cation and Anion Effects on Solvation Shell Dynamics'
items.quote: much faster than the H-bond exchange dynamics (∼2.5 ps).
items.confidenceNotes: Recent review (CC BY) summarising several independent experiments (Rezus & Bakker 2005, 2007 cited for the 2.5 ps anisotropy decay; also cited in a CC BY Frontiers in Chemistry 2024 review). Well established; approximate value.

items.labelEn: One reaction by one of the fastest enzymes (carbonic anhydrase)
items.labelFr: Une réaction par l’une des enzymes les plus rapides (anhydrase carbonique)
items.conditions: Record-holding enzymes such as carbonic anhydrase (CO2 + H2O ⇌ HCO3- + H+) carry out up to 10^6–10^7 reactions per second; time per reaction = 1 / rate. Value uses 10^6/s; low uses 10^7/s.
items.conditionsFr: Les enzymes championnes comme l’anhydrase carbonique (CO2 + H2O ⇌ HCO3- + H+) réalisent jusqu’à 10^6 à 10^7 réactions par seconde ; temps par réaction = 1 / cadence. Valeur pour 10^6/s ; borne basse pour 10^7/s.
items.locator: Section text after Figure 2 caption ('Rates vary immensely. Record holders are carbonic anhydrase…')
items.quote: These enzymes can carry out as many as 106-107 reactions per second.
items.confidenceNotes: '106-107' on the page is 10^6–10^7 with superscripts lost. The source groups carbonic anhydrase with superoxide dismutase; the value is a ceiling under saturating substrate, not a cellular rate. Value chosen at the 10^6 end, not a midpoint.

items.labelEn: One reaction by a typical enzyme
items.labelFr: Une réaction par une enzyme typique
items.conditions: Median turnover number (kcat) of metabolic enzymes, about 10 per second (literature compilation, BRENDA-based); time per reaction = 1 / kcat.
items.conditionsFr: Nombre de cycles catalytiques médian (kcat) des enzymes du métabolisme, environ 10 par seconde (compilation de la littérature, base BRENDA) ; temps par réaction = 1 / kcat.
items.locator: Paragraph on Figure 2A (distribution of kcat values, BNID 111411)
items.quote: the median kcat is about 10 s-1
items.confidenceNotes: Median of a wide distribution (orders of magnitude spread); 'about'. Underlying data: Bar-Even et al., Biochemistry 2011.

items.labelEn: Sugar (sucrose) breaking down in water on its own, without enzyme (half-life)
items.labelFr: Sucre (saccharose) qui se décompose seul dans l’eau, sans enzyme (demi-vie)
items.conditions: Spontaneous (uncatalysed) hydrolysis of sucrose in neutral water at 25 °C; extrapolated from rates measured at high temperature.
items.conditionsFr: Hydrolyse spontanée (non catalysée) du saccharose dans l’eau neutre à 25 °C ; extrapolée à partir de vitesses mesurées à haute température.
items.quote: The half-lives for spontaneous hydrolysis of trehalose and sucrose at 25 °C are 6.6 × 10 6 years and 440 years.
items.confidenceNotes: Single primary study, Arrhenius extrapolation from elevated temperatures. Same paper: invertase speeds this up enormously; good pedagogical contrast with the enzyme items.

excluded.reason: Opened and verified (half-life 2.3 × 10^9 years at 25 °C, Abstract), but left out to stay within 14 items; available if a very slow chemistry value is wanted (≈7e16 s).
